source_anchor: CLRS §9.1 minimum and maximum (linear-time scan); MDN Math.max with spread operator
prompt_text: Find the maximum value in [4, 7, 2, 9, 1, 5] and print it. Expected output: "9".

exec_cell.code: const a=[4,7,2,9,1,5]; let m=a[0]; for(let i=1;i<a.length;i++){if(a[i]>m)m=a[i];} console.log(m);

candidate_responses.text: CORRECT: Math.max with spread — built-in equivalent of the linear scan.
WRONG: loop terminates at i<floor(length/2), only inspecting the first half — misses the 9 at index 3.
candidate_responses.code: const a=[4,7,2,9,1,5]; let m=a[0]; for(let i=1;i<Math.floor(a.length/2);i++){if(a[i]>m)m=a[i];} console.log(m);

candidate_responses.text: CARGO-CULT: variable named "max", running scan structure intact, but the comparison is < instead of > so it tracks the minimum.
candidate_responses.code: const arr=[4,7,2,9,1,5]; let max=arr[0]; for(let i=1;i<arr.length;i++){if(arr[i]<max)max=arr[i];} console.log(max);
